name: boros aggro

winrate_basis.why: no head-to-head winrate exists for Modern in any source this repo can reach: statistics_matchups returns zero rows for the format and archetype, statistics_archetypes carries no winrate field, and this run's own fingerprint records winrate_vs_field as an empty map. Recording a number here would be inventing one.

opponent_gameplan: Curve Ocelot Pride or Ragavan into Guide of Souls energy and Ajani, Nacatl Pariah, then convert the board with Goblin Bombardment or a Voice of Victory turn where we are not allowed to respond.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Every threat is one or two mana and Voice of Victory stops us casting anything on their turn, so the game is decided before our five-drops are live.

key_cards.why: our opponents cannot cast spells during their turn - it turns off every counterspell and every flash creature we hold.
destroys a nonbasic land for two mana against a manabase that is seventeen nonbasics deep.
their own sweeper, brought in because our Frogs outclass their tokens in a long game.
one spell each turn caps a deck built to deploy a threat and hold up an answer.

primary_gameplan: Trade one-for-one early with Fatal Push and Orcish Bowmasters, then reset with Toxic Deluge once they have committed. Psychic Frog blocks a Ragavan all day and eats the cards Deluge would have wasted.
pitfalls: Force of Negation counters nothing in the maindeck worth countering: their threats are creatures.
Toxic Deluge for three kills our own Psychic Frog; cast it before deploying, not after.
Thoughtseize costs two life against a deck that wins at exactly that margin - it stays in only because Goblin Bombardment and Ajani are worth taking.
stance_rationale: Their board is wide and cheap - Ocelot Pride, Guide of Souls, Ragavan and Ajani tokens - so the answer is a sweeper rather than one-for-one removal. Toxic Deluge is that sweeper and it kills our own Psychic Frog and Orcish Bowmasters with it.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: {2}{R} 4/3 that destroys a nonbasic land on entry; we run seventeen and three basics.
one spell per turn, which is the tax a hold-up-interaction deck cannot pay.
sweeps our Psychic Frog and Orcish Bowmasters after they have committed to a board.
counters Force of Negation and evoked Subtlety, the two cards that let us interact while tapped out.

play_plan.keep: Two lands and two pieces of one-mana interaction; a threat-only hand loses on turn four.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Toxic Deluge, cast for two after they have committed the second wave.
play_plan.watch_for: Voice of Victory means our counters are dead on their turn - use the mana on our own.
play_plan.posture_why: Their curve ends before ours starts, so surviving to turn five is the whole game.

self_cost: Toxic Deluge for two or three takes every creature we control except a Psychic Frog that has already eaten cards, and except Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student, whose 0/3 body only dies to the three; Engineered Explosives at one still kills our own Tamiyo, since its destroy effect keys off mana value one rather than toughness.
